analysis.answer: Currently, each county determines whether to honor federal immigration detainer requests. This measure preempts that local authority, creating a uniform rule that no county jail may hold someone past their normal release time solely on such a detainer.

County jails that previously honored detainers will release individuals back into the community once their local custody reasons end. Federal immigration authorities will likely have to use more resources to apprehend targets in the community instead of taking custody directly at the jail.

The measure addresses concerns about unauthorized extended detention and the use of local resources for federal immigration enforcement. It may create a problem for federal immigration authorities, who argue that jail transfers are safer and more efficient than community apprehensions.

The state government gains authority over immigration detainer policy at the expense of county governments and local sheriffs. Immigrants subject to detainer requests gain protection from extended jail time.
